description: A webpack/rspack-based frontend toolchain for Lynx

members.name: buildDependencies
members.summary:
An array of files containing build dependencies.
Rspack will use the hash of each of these files to invalidate the persistent cache.
members.default: `['package.json', 'tsconfig.json' (or source.tsconfigPath), '.env', '.env.*', 'tailwindcss.config.*']`; when using the Rspeedy CLI with `performance.buildCache` enabled, the loaded `lynx.config.*` file is also added.

members.name: cacheDigest
members.summary:
Add additional cache digests, the previous build cache will be invalidated
when any value in the array changes.

members.name: cacheDirectory
members.summary: The output directory of the cache files.

exports.name: BundleFilenameContext
exports.summary: The context passed to the [`Filename.bundle`](api:Filename.bundle) function.

members.name: entryName
members.summary:
The name of the entry.

It is `undefined` for lazy bundles, since a lazy bundle name is resolved
per async chunk (use the `[name]` placeholder in the returned string
instead).

members.name: lazyBundle
members.summary:
Whether the filename is being resolved for a lazy bundle (async chunk)
instead of the main bundle of an entry.

This allows you to control the main bundle and the lazy bundles with a
single function, without needing a dedicated `lazyBundle` field.

members.name: platform
members.summary: The environment (platform) name, e.g. `'lynx'` or `'web'`.

members.name: override
members.summary: Custom Rspack chunk splitting config can be specified.

members.name: strategy
members.summary: The ChunkSplitting strategy.
members.remarks:
- `split-by-experience`(Rsbuild default): an empirical splitting strategy, automatically splits some commonly used npm packages into chunks of moderate size.

- `split-by-module`: split by NPM package granularity, each NPM package corresponds to a chunk.

- `split-by-size`: automatically split according to module size.

- `all-in-one`: bundle all codes into one chunk.

- `single-vendor`: bundle all NPM packages into a single chunk.

- `custom`: custom chunk splitting strategy.
members.default: In Rsbuild's default chunk splitting behavior, the strategy is `'split-by-experience'`.

members.name: maxSize
members.summary: The maximum size of a chunk, unit in bytes.

members.name: minSize
members.summary: The minimum size of a chunk, unit in bytes.

members.summary: `ChunkSplit.override`

members.name: strategy
members.summary: `ChunkSplit.strategy`

members.summary: `ChunkSplit.override`

members.summary: `ChunkSplit.strategy`

exports.name: Config
exports.summary: The `Config` is the configuration that `rspeedy` uses.

members.name: dev
members.summary: The [`Dev`](api:Dev) option is used to control the behavior related with development. Including: HMR, DevServer, etc.

members.name: environments
members.summary: The [`Config.environments`](api:Config.environments) option is used to set the output environment.
members.remarks: Normally you don't need this if you are not using Lynx for Web.
members.default: When this option is unset, Rspeedy passes `{ lynx: {} }` to Rsbuild.

members.name: mode
members.summary: Specify the build mode for Rsbuild and Rspack, as each mode has different default behavior and optimizations.
examples:
```ts
If the value of `mode` is `'development'`:

- Enable HMR and register the {@link https://rspack.rs/plugins/webpack/hot-module-replacement-plugin | HotModuleReplacementPlugin}.

- Generate JavaScript and CSS source maps. In Lynx environments, all `.map` assets are removed before emit. See {@link Output.sourceMap} for details.

- The `process.env.NODE_ENV` in the source code will be replaced with `'development'`.

- The `import.meta.env.MODE` in the source code will be replaced with `'development'`.

- The `import.meta.env.DEV` in the source code will be replaced with `true`.

- The `import.meta.env.PROD` in the source code will be replaced with `false`.
```

```ts
If the value of `mode` is `'production'`:

- Enable JavaScript code minification and register the {@link https://rspack.rs/plugins/rspack/swc-js-minimizer-rspack-plugin | SwcJsMinimizerRspackPlugin}.

- Generated JavaScript and CSS filenames will have hash suffixes, see {@link Output.filenameHash}.

- Generated CSS Modules classnames will be shorter, see {@link CssModules.localIdentName}.

- Generate JavaScript and CSS source maps. In Lynx environments, all `.map` assets are removed before emit. See {@link Output.sourceMap}.

- The `process.env.NODE_ENV` in the source code will be replaced with `'production'`.

- The `import.meta.env.MODE` in the source code will be replaced with `'production'`.

- The `import.meta.env.DEV` in the source code will be replaced with `false`.

- The `import.meta.env.PROD` in the source code will be replaced with `true`.
```
members.default:
Depends on `process.env.NODE_ENV`:

- `'production'` when `NODE_ENV` is `'production'`
- `'development'` when `NODE_ENV` is `'development'`
- `'none'` otherwise

With Rspeedy's CLI, `rspeedy dev` and `rspeedy preview` default to `'development'`, and `rspeedy build` defaults to `'production'`.

Possible values:

Only build specified environments.
For example, passing `['lynx']` will only build the `lynx` environment.
If not specified or passing an empty array, all environments will be built.

members.name: loadEnv
members.summary:
Rspeedy automatically loads the .env file by default, utilizing the [Rsbuild API](https://rsbuild.rs/api/javascript-api/core#load-env-variables).
You can use the environment variables defined in the .env file within your code by accessing them via `import.meta.env.FOO` or `process.env.Foo`.

members.name: loaderOptions
members.summary: `@lynx-js/css-extract-webpack-plugin#LoaderOptions`

members.name: pluginOptions
members.summary: `@lynx-js/css-extract-webpack-plugin#CssExtractRspackPluginOptions`

members.name: esModule
members.summary:
The same as [https://github.com/webpack-contrib/mini-css-extract-plugin#esModule](https://github.com/webpack-contrib/mini-css-extract-plugin#esModule).
By default, `@lynx-js/css-extract-webpack-plugin` generates JS modules that use the ES modules syntax.
There are some cases in which using ES modules is beneficial,
like in the case of module concatenation and tree shaking.

members.name: ignoreOrder

members.summary: `@lynx-js/css-extract-webpack-plugin#CssExtractRspackPluginOptions.pathinfo`

members.name: importLoaders
members.summary: The option `importLoaders` allows you to configure how many loaders before `css-loader` should be applied to `@imported` resources and CSS modules imports.
members.remarks: See [css-loader#import-loaders](https://github.com/webpack-contrib/css-loader?tab=readme-ov-file#importloaders) for details.
members.default: `1` when compiling CSS files and `2` when compiling Sass or Less files

members.name: modules
members.summary: The [`cssLoader.modules`](api:CssLoaderModules) option enables/disables the CSS Modules specification and setup basic behavior.
members.default: Enables CSS Modules with automatic `*.module.*` detection, camelCase exports, `namedExport: false`, and `localIdentName` inherited from `output.cssModules.localIdentName`.

members.name: auto
members.summary: `CssModules.auto`

members.name: exportLocalsConvention
members.summary: `CssModules.exportLocalsConvention`

members.name: localIdentName
members.summary: `CssModules.localIdentName`

members.name: namedExport
members.summary: Enables/disables ES modules named export for locals.

members.name: auto
members.summary: The `auto` option allows CSS modules to be automatically enabled based on their filenames.
members.remarks:
Given the various `auto` values, the behavior is described as follows:

- `true`: enable CSS modules for all files matching `/\.module\.\w+$/i.test(filename)` RegExp.

- `false`: disable CSS modules.

- `RegExp`: enable CSS modules for all files matching the `auto.test(filename)` RegExp.

- `function`: enable CSS modules based on the filter function.

See [css-loader#auto](https://github.com/webpack-contrib/css-loader?tab=readme-ov-file#auto) for details.

members.name: exportGlobals
members.summary: Allows exporting names from global class names, so you can use them via import.
members.remarks: See [css-loader#exportGlobals](https://github.com/webpack-contrib/css-loader?tab=readme-ov-file#exportglobals) for details.

members.name: exportLocalsConvention
members.summary: The style of exported class names.
members.remarks:
Given the various `exportLocalsConvention` values, the behavior is described as follows:

- `'asIs'`:	Class names will be exported as is.

- `'camelCase'`: Class names will be camelized, the original class name will not to be removed from the locals

- `'camelCaseOnly'`: Class names will be camelized, the original class name will be removed from the locals

- `'dashes'`: Only dashes in class names will be camelized

- `'dashesOnly'`: Dashes in class names will be camelized, the original class name will be removed from the locals

See [css-loader#exportLocalsConvention](https://github.com/webpack-contrib/css-loader?tab=readme-ov-file#exportlocalsconvention) for details.

members.name: localIdentName
members.summary: Sets the format of the className generated by CSS Modules after compilation.
members.remarks:
Available placeholders:

- `[local]`: Original class name

- `[hash]`: Hash of the class name

- `[path]`: File path

- `[name]`: File name

- `[ext]`: File extension

See [css-loader#localIdentName](https://github.com/webpack-contrib/css-loader?tab=readme-ov-file#localIdentName) for details.

members.name: version
members.summary: Specify the decorator syntax version to be used.
members.remarks: If you want to know the differences between different decorators versions, you can refer to: [How does this proposal compare to other versions of decorators?](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-decorators?tab=readme-ov-file#how-does-this-proposal-compare-to-other-versions-of-decorators)

members.name: assetPrefix
members.summary: The [`Dev.assetPrefix`](api:Dev.assetPrefix) is used to set the URL prefix for static assets during development.
members.remarks:
During `rspeedy dev`, if this option is not set to `false`, the dev plugin normalizes it to `http://<detected-host>:<port>/` and appends `server.base` when configured.

The functionality of [`Dev.assetPrefix`](api:Dev.assetPrefix) is basically the same as the [output.publicPath](https://rspack.rs/config/output#outputpublicpath)
config in Rspack. With the following differences:

- `dev.assetPrefix` only takes effect during development.

- `dev.assetPrefix` automatically appends a trailing `/` by default.

- The value of `dev.assetPrefix` is written to the `process.env.ASSET_PREFIX` environment variable.

members.name: hmr
members.summary: Whether to enable Hot Module Replacement (HMR).
members.remarks:
By default, Rspeedy uses HMR as the preferred method to update modules. If HMR is disabled or cannot be used in certain scenarios, it will automatically fallback to [`Dev.liveReload`](api:Dev.liveReload).

To completely disable both HMR and live reload, set both `dev.hmr` and `dev.liveReload` to `false`. Then, no WebSocket requests will be made to the dev server on the page, and the page will not automatically refresh when file changes.

members.name: liveReload
members.summary: Whether to enable live reload functionality.
members.default:
true

Live reload is used as a fallback when [`Dev.hmr`](api:Dev.hmr) is disabled or cannot be used in certain scenarios. When enabled, the page will automatically refresh when source files are changed.

To completely disable both HMR and live reload, set both `dev.hmr` and `dev.liveReload` to `false`. Then, no WebSocket requests will be made to the dev server on the page, and the page will not automatically refresh when file changes.

members.name: progressBar
members.summary: Whether to display progress bar during compilation.

members.name: watchFiles
members.summary: Watch specified files and directories for changes. When a file change is detected, it can trigger a page reload or restart the dev server.

members.name: writeToDisk
members.summary: Used to control whether the build artifacts of the development environment are written to the disk.
members.remarks:
This is bypassed to [`webpack-dev-middleware`](https://github.com/webpack/webpack-dev-middleware?tab=readme-ov-file#writetodisk).

Setting `writeToDisk: true` won't change the behavior of the `webpack-dev-middleware`, and bundle files accessed through the browser will still be served from memory.

This option also accepts a `Function` value, which can be used to filter which files are written to disk.

The function follows the same premise as `Array#filter` in which a return value of `false` will not write the file, and a return value of `true` will write the file to disk.

exports.name: EntryDescription
exports.summary: The `EntryDescription` describes a entry. It is useful when the project has multiple entries with different configuration.
exports.remarks:
It is similar with the [Entry Description Object](https://rspack.rs/config/entry#entry-description-object) of Rspack.
But only a few properties that Lynx supports is allowed.

members.name: backgroundOptions
members.summary:
[`Minify.backgroundOptions`](api:Minify.backgroundOptions) is used to override
[`Minify.jsOptions`](api:Minify.jsOptions) for background-thread bundles.
members.remarks:
This option is deep-merged into [`Minify.jsOptions`](api:Minify.jsOptions).
It is mainly used together with ReactLynx dual-thread outputs so that
main-thread and background-thread bundles can use different compress rules.

members.name: css
members.summary: Whether enable the CSS minification.
members.remarks: When building for production, [@rsbuild/plugin-css-minimizer](https://github.com/rspack-contrib/rsbuild-plugin-css-minimizer) is used to minify CSS assets for better transmission efficiency.
members.default: When `output.minify` is enabled and `css` is unset, this defaults to `true`.

members.name: js
members.summary: Whether enable the JavaScript minification.
members.default: When `output.minify` is enabled and `js` is unset, this defaults to `true`.

members.name: jsOptions
members.summary: [`Minify.jsOptions`](api:Minify.jsOptions) is used to configure SWC minification options.
members.remarks: For detailed configurations, please refer to [SwcJsMinimizerRspackPlugin](https://rspack.rs/plugins/rspack/swc-js-minimizer-rspack-plugin).
members.default: When JavaScript minification is enabled and `jsOptions` is unset, this defaults to `{}`.

members.name: mainThreadOptions
members.summary:
[`Minify.mainThreadOptions`](api:Minify.mainThreadOptions) is used to override
[`Minify.jsOptions`](api:Minify.jsOptions) for main-thread bundles.
members.remarks:
This option is deep-merged into [`Minify.jsOptions`](api:Minify.jsOptions).
It is mainly used together with ReactLynx dual-thread outputs so that
main-thread and background-thread bundles can use different compress rules.

members.name: assetPrefix
members.summary: The [`Output.assetPrefix`](api:Output.assetPrefix) is used to set the URL prefix for static assets.
members.remarks:
The functionality of [`Output.assetPrefix`](api:Output.assetPrefix) is basically the same as the [output.publicPath](https://rspack.rs/config/output#outputpublicpath)
config in Rspack. With the following differences:

- `output.assetPrefix` only takes effect in the production build.

- `output.assetPrefix` automatically appends a trailing `/` by default.

- The value of `output.assetPrefix` is written to the `process.env.ASSET_PREFIX` environment variable.

members.name: cleanDistPath
members.summary: The [`Output.cleanDistPath`](api:Output.cleanDistPath) option determines whether all files in the output directory (default: `dist`) are removed before the build starts.
members.remarks:
By default, if the output directory is a subdirectory of the project root path, Rspeedy will automatically clean all files in the build directory.

When [output.distPath.root](https://rsbuild.rs/config/output/dist-path#root-directory) is an external directory or the same as the project root directory, `cleanDistPath` is not enabled by default to prevent accidental deletion of files from other directories.
members.default: Automatically enabled when `output.distPath.root` is a subdirectory of the project root; otherwise disabled.

members.name: copy
members.summary: The [`Output.copy`](api:Output.copy) option is used for copying files to the dist directory.
members.remarks: For more options, see [Rspack.CopyRspackPlugin](https://rspack.rs/plugins/rspack/copy-rspack-plugin).

members.name: cssModules
members.summary: The [`CssModules`](api:CssModules) option is used for the customization of CSS Modules configurations.
members.remarks:
The CSS module is enabled for `*.module.css`, `*.module.scss` and `*.module.less`.
Use [`CssModules.auto`](api:CssModules.auto) to customize the filtering behavior.

members.name: dataUriLimit
members.summary: The [`Output.dataUriLimit`](api:Output.dataUriLimit) option is used to set the size threshold to inline static assets such as images and fonts.

members.name: distPath
members.summary: Set the directory of the dist files.
members.remarks: More options can be found at [Rsbuild - distPath](https://rsbuild.rs/config/output/dist-path).
members.default: Uses Rsbuild's default distPath configuration with `root: 'dist'`.

members.name: filename
members.summary: The [`Filename`](api:Filename) determines the name of the JavaScript bundle file to be output. These bundles will be written to the directory specified by output.path.
members.remarks: If a string is provided, it will be used as [`Filename.bundle`](api:Filename.bundle).

members.name: filenameHash
members.summary: The [`Output.filenameHash`](api:Output.filenameHash) option controls whether to add a hash value to the filename after the production build.
members.remarks: [`Output.filename`](api:Output.filename) has a higher priority than [`Output.filenameHash`](api:Output.filenameHash).
members.default: In production web builds, Rsbuild defaults this option to `true`; development builds and non-web outputs omit hashes by default.

members.name: inlineScripts
members.summary: The [`Output.inlineScripts`](api:Output.inlineScripts) option controls whether to inline scripts into Lynx bundle (`.lynx.bundle`).
members.remarks:
This is different with [output.inlineScripts](https://rsbuild.rs/config/output/inline-scripts) since we normally want to inline scripts in Lynx bundle (`.lynx.bundle`).

There are two points that need to be especially noted:

1. Only background thread scripts can remain non-inlined, whereas the main thread script is always inlined.

2. Currently, when `experimental_isLazyBundle` is enabled, `inlineScripts` will always be `true`.
members.default: Rspeedy defaults this to `true` and only switches it to `false` when the user explicitly enables the top-level `splitChunks` option.

members.name: legalComments
members.summary: The [`Output.legalComments`](api:Output.legalComments) controls how to handle the legal comment.
members.remarks:
This is different with Rsbuild since we normally do not want a `.LEGAL.txt` file in Lynx outputs.

This behavior can be configured by using one of the following options:

- `linked`: Extract all legal comments to a `.LEGAL.txt` file and link to them with a comment.

- `inline`: Preserve all legal comments in original position.

- `none`: Remove all legal comments.

members.name: minify
members.summary: The [`Minify`](api:Minify) configures whether to enable code minification in the production build, or to configure minimizer options.

members.name: sourceMap
members.summary: The [`SourceMap`](api:SourceMap) configures whether and how to generate source-map for outputs.
members.default: When this option is unset in Lynx builds, JavaScript source maps use `'cheap-module-source-map'` in development and `'source-map'` in production; CSS source maps are also generated. All `.map` assets are removed before emit.

members.name: buildCache
members.summary: Enable or configure persistent build cache.
members.default:
```ts
false

@beta This feature is experimental and may be changed in the future.
```

members.name: chunkSplit
members.summary: [`Performance.chunkSplit`](api:Performance.chunkSplit) is used to configure the chunk splitting strategy.
members.default:
For web builds, Rsbuild currently uses `{ strategy: 'split-by-experience' }` when this option is unset.

 Use the top-level [`Config.splitChunks`](api:Config.splitChunks) option instead.

members.name: printFileSize
members.summary: Whether to print the file sizes after production build.

members.name: profile
members.summary: Whether capture timing information in Lynx runtime integrations such as ReactLynx.
examples:
Enable profile.

- Frameworks like ReactLynx will include runtime information using `console.profile`.
- Rspeedy will emit `dist/stats.json` after build for bundle analysis compatibility.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from '@lynx-js/rspeedy'

export default defineConfig({
  performance: { profile: true },
})
```
members.default: Rspeedy sets this to `true` when `DEBUG` contains `rspeedy`; otherwise it leaves the option unset.

members.name: removeConsole
members.summary: Whether to remove `console.[methodName]` in production build.

members.name: alias
members.summary: Create aliases to `import` or `require` certain modules more easily.

members.name: aliasStrategy
members.summary:
Set the strategy for path alias resolution, to control the priority relationship
between the `paths` option in `tsconfig.json` and the `resolve.alias` option of Rsbuild.
members.default:
`'prefer-tsconfig'`

- `prefer-tsconfig` (default): The `paths` option in `tsconfig.json` will take precedence over the
`resolve.alias` option of Rsbuild.
- `prefer-alias`: The `resolve.alias` option of Rsbuild will take precedence over the
`paths` option in `tsconfig.json`.

members.name: dedupe
members.summary: Force to resolve the specified packages from project root, which is useful for deduplicating packages and reducing the bundle size.
members.remarks:
[`Resolve.dedupe`](api:Resolve.dedupe) is implemented based on [`Resolve.alias`](api:Resolve.alias), it will get the path of the specified package through `require.resolve` in the project root directory and set it to the alias.

The alias generated by [`Resolve.dedupe`](api:Resolve.dedupe) will be merged with the configured [`Resolve.alias`](api:Resolve.alias) in the project, and the [`Resolve.alias`](api:Resolve.alias) config will take precedence when the keys are the same.

members.name: extensions
members.summary: Automatically resolve file extensions when importing modules. This means you can import files without explicitly writing their extensions.
members.remarks:
The difference between `resolve.extensions` and `tools.rspack.resolve.extensions`:

`resolve.extensions`: Completely overrides Rspeedy's default resolution.

`tools.rspack.resolve.extensions`: Merges with the default configuration using [`webpack-merge`](https://github.com/survivejs/webpack-merge).
members.default:
`['.ts', '.tsx', '.mjs', '.js', '.jsx', '.json', '.cjs']`

For example, if importing './index', Rsbuild will try to resolve using the following order:

- `./index.ts`

- `./index.tsx`

- `./index.mjs`

- `./index.js`

- `./index.jsx`

- `./index.json`

- `./index.cjs`

exports.name: RsdoctorRspackPluginOptions
exports.summary:
Simplified options type for `tools.rsdoctor`.

Keep this type free of deeply nested/intersection utility types to ensure
typia can generate validators from `Config`.

members.name: linter
members.type: { extends?: unknown[]; level?: "Ignore" | "Warn" | "Error"; rules?: Record<string, unknown> }

members.name: base
members.summary: Configure the base path of the server.
members.remarks:
Users can access lynx bundle through `http://<host>:<port>/main.lynx.bundle` by default.

If you want to access lynx bundle through `http://<host>:<port>/foo/main.lynx.bundle`, you can change `server.base` to `/foo`

you can refer to [server.base](https://rsbuild.rs/config/server/base) for more information.

members.name: compress
members.summary: Configure whether to enable [gzip compression](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/gzip_compression) for static assets served by the dev server or preview server.

members.name: cors
members.summary: Configure CORS for the dev server or preview server.
members.default:
Uses Rsbuild's default CORS options.

- Set to an object to enable CORS with the specified options.

- Set to `true` to enable CORS with the default options (allows all origins, not recommended).

- Set to `false` to disable CORS.

See [Rsbuild - server.cors](https://rsbuild.rs/config/server/cors) for details.

members.name: headers
members.summary: Adds headers to all responses.

members.name: host
members.summary: Specify the host that the Rspeedy Server listens to.
members.remarks: During `rspeedy dev`, if `server.host` is unset, the dev plugin keeps the server bound to the IPv4 wildcard address while resolving dev-server-related URLs and client host settings with a detected non-loopback IPv4 address, such as `192.168.1.50`. If no eligible IPv4 address exists, it binds to the IPv6 wildcard address and uses a detected IPv6 address for URLs. It falls back to an IPv4 loopback URL when no non-loopback IP is available. If you have multiple network interfaces, set `server.host` explicitly to choose the desired address.

members.name: port
members.summary: Specify the port that the Rspeedy Server listens to.
members.remarks: By default, the server automatically increments the port number when the configured port is occupied.

members.name: proxy
members.summary: Configure proxy rules for the dev server or preview server to proxy requests to the specified service.

members.name: strictPort
members.summary: When a port is occupied, Rspeedy will automatically increment the port number until an available port is found.
members.default:
```ts
false

By default, strict port mode is disabled. Set strictPort to true and Rspeedy will throw an exception when the port is occupied.
```

members.name: alias
members.summary:
`Resolve.alias`

 - Use [`Resolve.alias`](api:Resolve.alias) instead.

members.name: assetsInclude
members.summary: Include additional files that should be treated as static assets.
members.remarks:
By default, Rsbuild treats common image, font, audio, and video files as static assets.
Through the source.assetsInclude config, you can specify additional file types that should be treated as static assets.
These added static assets are processed using the same rules as the built-in supported static assets。

The usage of `source.assetsInclude` is consistent with [Condition](https://rspack.rs/config/module#condition)
in Rspack, which supports passing in strings, regular expressions, arrays of conditions, or logical conditions
to match the module path or assets.

members.name: decorators
members.summary: Used to configure the decorators syntax.
members.remarks: See [`Decorators.version`](api:Decorators.version) for more information.

members.name: define
members.summary: The `define` options is used to define some values or expressions at compile time.
members.remarks:
- If the value provided is a string, it will be utilized as a code fragment.

- If the value provided is an object, all its keys will be defined in the same manner.

- If the value isn't a string, it will be stringified, with functions included.

- Notably, if a `typeof` prefix is attached to the key, it will be exclusively defined for `typeof` calls."

members.name: entry
members.summary: The [`Entry`](api:Entry) option is used to set the entry module.

members.name: exclude
members.summary: The `source.exclude` is used to specify JavaScript files that should be excluded from compilation.
members.remarks:
By default, Rsbuild compiles JavaScript files in the current directory and TypeScript/JSX files
in all directories. Through the `source.exclude` config, you can specify files or directories
that should be excluded from compilation.
The usage of `source.exclude` is consistent with [Rule.exclude](https://rspack.rs/config/module#ruleexclude)
in Rspack, which supports passing in strings or regular expressions to match module paths.

members.name: include
members.summary: The `source.include` is used to specify additional JavaScript files that need to be compiled.
members.remarks:
To avoid redundant compilation, by default, Rsbuild only compiles JavaScript
files in the current directory and TypeScript and JSX files in all directories.
It does not compile JavaScript files under `node_modules`.

Through the `source.include` config, you can specify directories or modules
that need to be compiled by Rsbuild.
The usage of `source.include` is consistent with [Rule.include](https://rspack.rs/config/module#ruleinclude)
in Rspack, which supports passing in strings or regular expressions to match the module path.
members.default: When unset, Rsbuild compiles JavaScript files in the current directory and TypeScript or JSX files in all directories, while excluding JavaScript files under `node_modules`.

members.name: preEntry
members.summary:
Add a script before the entry file of each page. This script will be executed before the page code.
It can be used to execute global logics, such as injecting polyfills, setting global styles, etc.
members.remarks: See [source.preEntry](https://rsbuild.rs/config/source/pre-entry) for more details.

members.name: transformImport
members.summary: The [`TransformImport`](api:TransformImport) option transforms the import paths to enable modular imports from subpaths of third-party packages, similar to the functionality provided by [babel-plugin-import](https://npmjs.com/package/babel-plugin-import).

members.name: tsconfigPath
members.summary: Configure a custom `tsconfig.json` file path to use, can be a relative or absolute path.
members.remarks:
The `tsconfigPath` configuration affects the following behaviors:

- The `paths` field is used to configure [`Path Aliases`](api:Source.alias).

- Sets the scope and rules for the [Type Check Plugin](https://rsbuild.rs/guide/basic/typescript#type-checking).

members.name: css
members.summary: Whether to generate CSS source maps.
members.remarks:
Lynx environments enable CSS source maps so that CSS diagnostics can be
mapped back to the source; all `.map` assets are removed before emit.

members.name: js
members.summary: How the source map should be generated. Setting it to `false` will disable the source map.
members.remarks: See [Rspack - Devtool](https://rspack.rs/config/devtool) for details.
members.default: When `output.sourceMap` is an object and `js` is unset, it defaults to `'cheap-module-source-map'` in development. In production, it defaults to `'source-map'` for Lynx environments and `false` otherwise.

members.name: bundlerChain
members.summary: The [`Tools.bundlerChain`](api:Tools.bundlerChain) changes the options of [Rspack](https://rspack.rs) using [rspack-chain](https://github.com/rspack-contrib/rspack-chain).

members.name: cssExtract
members.summary: The [`CssExtract`](api:CssExtract) controls the options of [CssExtractRspackPlugin](https://rspack.rs/plugins/rspack/css-extract-rspack-plugin)

members.name: cssLoader
members.summary: The [`CssLoader`](api:CssLoader) controls the options of [css-loader](https://github.com/webpack-contrib/css-loader).
members.default: Uses defaults derived from `output.cssModules` and `output.sourceMap`, with `importLoaders` set to `1` for CSS files and `2` for Sass/Less files.

members.name: rsdoctor
members.summary: The [`Tools.rsdoctor`](api:Tools.rsdoctor) controls the options of [Rsdoctor](https://rsdoctor.dev/).
members.remarks: Setting `RSDOCTOR=true` enables Rsdoctor. When it is enabled, Rspeedy merges additional plugin defaults during config normalization.

members.name: rspack
members.summary: The [`Tools.rspack`](api:Tools.rspack) controls the options of [Rspack](https://rspack.rs/).

members.name: swc
members.summary: The [`Tools.swc`](api:Tools.swc) controls the options of [builtin:swc-loader](https://rspack.rs/guide/features/builtin-swc-loader).

members.name: camelToDashComponentName
members.summary: Whether to convert camelCase imports to kebab-case.
examples:
- Input:

```js
import { ButtonGroup } from 'foo'
```

- Output:

When set to `true`:
```js
import ButtonGroup from 'foo/button-group'
```

When set to `false`:
```js
import ButtonGroup from 'foo/ButtonGroup'
```

members.name: customName
members.summary: Customize the transformed path.
members.remarks:
You you can specify the format of the transformed path.
For example, by setting it to `my-lib/{{ camelCase member }}`, you can convert the member into camelCase.

The following formats are supported:

- `kebabCase`: lowercase letters, words joined by hyphens. For example: `my-variable-name`.

- `snakeCase`: lowercase letters, words joined by underscores. For example: `my_variable_name`.

- `camelCase`: first letter lowercase, the first letter of each following word uppercase. For example: `myVariableName`.

- `upperCase`: uppercase letters, other characters unchanged. For example: `MY-VARIABLE-NAME`.

- `lowerCase`: lowercase letters, other characters unchanged. For example: `my-variable-name`.

members.name: libraryDirectory
members.summary: Used to splice the transformed path, the splicing rule is `${libraryName}/${libraryDirectory}/${member}`, where member is the imported member.
examples:
- Input:

```js
import { Button } from 'foo'
```

- Output:

```js
import Button from 'foo/lib/button'
```

members.name: libraryName
members.summary: The original import path that needs to be transformed.
members.remarks: This option is required.

members.name: transformToDefaultImport
members.summary: Whether to convert import statements to default imports.
examples:
- Input:

```js
import { Button } from 'foo'
```

- Output:

When set to `true`:
```js
import Button from 'foo/button'
```

When set to `false`:
```js
import { Button } from 'foo/button'
```
